question: Who among the following established the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Vivekananda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Swami Vivekananda founded the **Ramakrishna Mission** in 1897 to carry out social service and educational work.

• The mission was named after his guru, **Ramakrishna Paramahamsa**, and its motto is "For one's own salvation, and for the welfare of the world."

• The headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission is located at **Belur Math** in West Bengal, India.

• The mission operates various educational institutions, hospitals, and rural development programs to promote social and economic upliftment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Swami Vivekananda**

• Born as Narendranath Datta on 12 January 1863, Swami Vivekananda was a chief disciple of the Indian mystic Ramakrishna.

• He played a key role in introducing the Indian philosophies of Vedanta and Yoga to the Western world.

• Vivekananda is best known for his speech at the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago in 1893, where he began his address with "Sisters and brothers of America."

• He emphasized the importance of selfless service and the spiritual unity of all religions.

• **Ramakrishna Paramahamsa**

• Born as Gadadhar Chattopadhyay in 1836, Ramakrishna was a renowned Indian mystic and saint.

• He experienced spiritual ecstasies from a young age and became a priest at the Dakshineswar Kali Temple.

• Ramakrishna's teachings emphasized the unity of all religions and the pursuit of God-realization through devotion and meditation.

• His disciples, including Swami Vivekananda, spread his teachings and established several religious and social organizations.

• **Belur Math**

• Belur Math is the headquarters of the Ramakrishna Math and Mission, located on the west bank of the Hooghly River in Howrah, West Bengal.

• The site was chosen by Swami Vivekananda, and the campus includes temples dedicated to Ramakrishna, Sarada Devi, and Swami Vivekananda.

• Belur Math is known for its distinctive architecture that harmonizes Hindu, Christian, and Islamic motifs to symbolize the unity of all religions.

• It serves as a center for spiritual learning, social service, and cultural activities.
